A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text and Appendices A–D. Algorithms, equations and proofs can be matched reliably across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical regret bounds and proofs, including its game applications. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. Its added lower-bound construction and computational analysis are mathematical results, not experiments or simulations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 6 replaces the weighted mixture of Q matrices with computations using V_t, c_t, C_t and S_t, targeting quadratic instead of cubic update time. This changes the computational procedure while preserving its intended output; the prior, meta-learning framework, BM reduction and game-learning rules remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts empirical task evaluations. The expert problems and game classes remain theoretical settings; the new lower-bound construction is not an evaluated test scenario.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. The added efficiency comparison with prior algorithms concerns theoretical complexity.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics or training budgets are reported in either version.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments or empirical case studies. The additional lower-bound analysis belongs to the theoretical development.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experiments, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical result entries or qualitative experimental findings. The revised running-time guarantee and added lower bound are theoretical changes assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds a dummy-expert construction arguing for an Omega(sqrt(c_phi T log c_phi)) lower bound across intermediate comparator complexities. Appendix B.3.2 substantially revises Theorem B.4 and its proof, changing Algorithm 6's stated per-iteration complexity from O(d^3) to O(d^2). The principal regret and game-convergence upper bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: improved comparator-adaptive regret bounds, two efficient prior-aware approaches, and accelerated adaptive convergence for the specified class of games.

C2.justification: The new Section 3 discussion interprets the complexity dependence as tight beyond the standard external, internal and swap-regret cases. The restrictions to nonnegative-social-external-regret games and the unwanted additive N^2 log d term remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3.2 replaces the implementation pseudocode and explains how shared products allow the new intermediate quantities to be computed in quadratic time. No code-access information, hardware details or empirical implementation settings are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhao et al. (2024) as inspiration for the stability correction in Section 6. Section 4 also newly positions the quadratic implementation as matching the efficiency of Blum and Mansour (2007) and Lu et al. (2025).

P1.justification: The revision adds a localized optimality discussion, expands the implementation derivation and makes small wording corrections, including 'comparative-adaptive' to 'comparator-adaptive.' The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Algorithm boxes are restyled, Algorithm 6 is redesigned around the new formulas, and existing algorithms and equations reflow across pages. No figures or result tables are added.

improvement.justification: The quadratic kernelized update and added lower-bound argument provide useful improvements to computational efficiency and optimality support while retaining the main guarantees. These gains are tempered by an implementation omission: the new Algorithm 6 divides by d−2 without specifying a d=2 special case, unlike the earlier formulation.
